Amazon Detailed Interview Experience!
𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: Base 19.5 LPA , 6.5 L Sign on Bonus Year-1 + 5.18 Sign on bonus Year-2, RSU 15.56 L (Vested in 4 years)
𝐏𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: SDE1
𝐂𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐠𝐞: Not from well known (Can’t disclose the name)
𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐨𝐫 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞: 2 yrs 3 months (Worked in Service based company)
𝐀𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐝: HR directly reached out on LinkedIn

𝐑𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝-𝟏 𝐎𝐧𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐀𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭
DSA Q-1 A medium-level problem based on strings and sorting.
DSA Q-2 A hard-level problem based on graphs.
Other: Multiple-choice questions based on Amazon Leadership Principles.
𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞:Candidate solved all 2 dsa questions and received an interview call.

𝐑𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝-𝟐 𝐃𝐒𝐀 + 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 (𝐁𝐞𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐥)
DSA Q-1 Rotten Orange (BFS + Matrix, medium)
Ref: https://lnkd.in/g6RBg_th
DSA Q-2 Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum (Dp + Tree, Hard)
Ref: https://lnkd.in/g2xSPCJq
𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞: Candidate could complete all two questions with optimal TC. 
𝐅𝐞𝐞𝐝𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐝: Good on coding questions but mixed for the Amazon Leadership Principles.

𝐑𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝-𝟑 𝐃𝐒𝐀 + 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 (𝐁𝐞𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐥)
DSA Q-1 Walls and Gates (Grid Multi Source BFS, Medium)
Ref: https://lnkd.in/gKXJ978T
DSA Q-2 Group Anagrams (Hashing , Medium)
Ref: https://lnkd.in/gSZX3R2w 
Candidate was also asked 2-3 leadership questions. 
𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞: Candidate could complete all two questions with optimal TC. 
𝐅𝐞𝐞𝐝𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐝: Coding and Leadership both were positive this time.

𝐑𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝-𝟒 𝐃𝐒𝐀 + 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 (𝐁𝐞𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐥)
DSA Q-1 Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling (Binary Search + DP, Hard)
Ref: https://lnkd.in/gNXiinWG 
Candidate was asked 4-5 leadership questions.
𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞: Completed DSA question in optimal TC and answered leadership questions using STAR method relating to his personal past experiences. 
𝐅𝐞𝐞𝐝𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐝: Wait for the final results! Most impatient moments 😰😨

Candidate received an offer from Amazon 🥳🥳! 

𝐍𝐨𝐭𝐞: DSA questions were pretty standard but were of medium-hard leetcode level. Leadership principles are very important to get into Amazon, don't neglect this.

Stay tuned for more such detailed interview experiences🙌.

#InterviewExperience #Amazon #FAANG #SDE1
…see more

ai_analysis.summary: The post summarizes an Amazon SDE1 interview process for a candidate with 2 years and 3 months of prior experience. The process included one online assessment with two DSA questions and Amazon Leadership Principles multiple-choice questions, followed by four rounds combining DSA and leadership interviews. The named problems covered strings, sorting, graphs, matrices, trees, grids, hashing, breadth-first search, dynamic programming, and binary search, but the post does not provide algorithm implementations. The candidate ultimately received an offer and emphasizes that both medium-to-hard DSA preparation and Amazon Leadership Principles were important.

interview_questions.question: What was included in the Amazon SDE1 online assessment described in the post?
interview_questions.answer:
The assessment contained a medium-level string and sorting problem and a hard-level graph problem.
It also contained multiple-choice questions about Amazon Leadership Principles.
The candidate solved both DSA questions and received an interview call.

interview_questions.question: Which techniques does the post associate with the two Round 2 DSA problems?
interview_questions.answer:
Rotten Orange is associated with breadth-first search and a matrix.
Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum is associated with dynamic programming and a tree.

interview_questions.question: Which medium-level Round 3 problems were asked, and what techniques were named for them?
interview_questions.answer:
Walls and Gates was associated with grid multi-source breadth-first search.
Group Anagrams was associated with hashing.

interview_questions.question: Which algorithm techniques were identified for Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling?
interview_questions.answer:
The problem was labeled hard.
The post identifies binary search and dynamic programming as its techniques.

interview_questions.question: How did the candidate answer the leadership questions in Round 4?
interview_questions.answer:
The candidate answered four to five leadership questions using the STAR method.
The answers drew on the candidate's personal past experiences.
